newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West spot power drops amid excess supplies.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West spot power drops amid excess supplies.

text.p: Spot power prices in the western U.S. fell again on Friday, ending a week marked by an increasingly bearish supply/demand outlook.

"Snow is expected at the Canada-Washington state border over the weekend," said one Northwest trader. "Temperatures are below average, and precipitation is above average. It is looking more and more like we might have the same type of water year we had last year."
Daily prices at the California-Oregon border were quoted at $14.00 per megawatt hour (MWh) for Saturday and $15.00 for Monday, down slightly from at $14.75-15.25 on Thursday.
"Things were looking up early this month when Bonneville pulled out of the market, but now it is quite a bit weaker," said an over-the-counter trader.
"Back then fourth-quarter was going for over $17.00, now you are lucky to sell at $16.40."

For Monday pre-scheduled sales, Bonneville Power Administration raised prices for heavy-load hours to as high as $20.00 MWh, compared with $17.00 for Friday sales. Sales for hours 1000-2100 PDT were capped at 200 MW.
But trade sources said the BPA prices were way above the market and indicate only that the federal power marketing agency does not have a big need to sell surplus generation.
Spot Southwest power prices also slipped lower Friday, with Monday Palo Verde quoted $19.00-20.00, down from $20.00-21.00 on Thursday.
October COB was last quoted $15.25-15.75 MWh, down from $15.50-16.00 on Thursday. October Palo Verde was last quoted $15.75-16.25 MWh, unchanged from Thursday.
